## 2. Room-by-Room Packing Checklist

### Packing timeline
| When | What to pack |
|---|---|
| Weeks 6-5 | Storage, garage, off-season clothes, books, decor, extra linens |
| Weeks 4-3 | Guest room, office, dining room, wall art, most of the kitchen |
| Weeks 2-1 | Living room, bedrooms, bathroom backups, pantry |
| Final 2-3 days | Daily-use items, bathroom, bedding, remaining kitchen |

**General rules:** Label every box on the **top and two sides** with room + contents. Number boxes and keep a running inventory. Put heavy items in small boxes and light ones in large. Keep one "do not pack" area for the open-first box and document folder.

### Kitchen
- [ ] Declutter: duplicate utensils, mismatched containers, expired spices and pantry items
- [ ] Wrap dishes vertically, with padding between each
- [ ] Glasses and stemware in dividers or wrapped individually
- [ ] Knives sheathed and labeled "SHARP"
- [ ] Use up or donate perishables and open liquids
- [ ] Keep out: 2 plates/bowls/mugs, a pan, a knife, coffee supplies
- [ ] Movers generally won't take open food, cleaning chemicals, or aerosols. Ask your mover for the exact list.

### Living Room
- [ ] Pad and wrap TV/electronics; photograph cable connections before unplugging
- [ ] Bag cords, label them, and tape them to the device
- [ ] Wrap lamps separately; pack shades in boxes
- [ ] Bubble-wrap or blanket artwork and mirrors; use mirror boxes
- [ ] Books in small boxes only

### Bedrooms
- [ ] Declutter closets: donate anything unworn in a year
- [ ] Keep clothes on hangers in wardrobe boxes if your mover supplies them, or use trash bags over hangers
- [ ] Dresser drawers: remove breakables; light clothes can stay if the mover allows it
- [ ] Disassemble beds; bag and label hardware, taped to the frame
- [ ] Keep out: 1 week of clothes, bedding, toiletries, chargers

### Bathrooms
- [ ] Toss expired meds, cosmetics, and half-empty bottles
- [ ] Seal liquids in zip bags
- [ ] Pack towels as padding
- [ ] Keep out: toiletries, TP, medications, shower curtain

### Office
- [ ] Back up computers; carry laptops yourself
- [ ] Shred old paperwork; scan and keep key documents digitally
- [ ] Photograph desktop setups before unplugging
- [ ] Keep out: laptops, hard drives, important documents

### Garage / Basement / Storage
- [ ] Declutter first. This is where the most money and weight is saved.
- [ ] Drain gas and oil from mowers and trimmers
- [ ] Dispose of paint, propane, chemicals, and batteries per local rules; movers usually can't carry hazmat
- [ ] Bundle tools and label them
- [ ] Check whether large items (grill, bikes, ladders) are worth the shipping weight

### Dog items
- [ ] Pack what you can't buy fast: bed, crate, toys, medications, food
- [ ] Keep the dog's gear in your car, not the truck

### Declutter tips
- **Weight is money.** Movers charge by weight or space. Every box you skip saves cash.
- **The one-year rule:** if you haven't used it in a year, sell or donate it.
- **Replace vs. move:** cheap furniture, old mattresses, and bulky low-value items often cost more to ship than to replace.
- **Sell early:** list larger items 4-6 weeks out. Use Facebook Marketplace or local groups. Donate the rest by week 2.
- **Donation pickups** book up in summer, so schedule them by week 3. Ask for receipts.
- **Hazardous items:** dispose of these before packing day.
- **Photograph high-value items** and keep their serial numbers.
